title: Kali Uchis Rides a Carriage Onstage and Teases a New Album!
summary: Picture this: a music festival, a huge stage, and suddenly — a carriage rolls out carrying a superstar. That's how Kali Uchis kicked off her For the Girls tour at Sueños 2026 in Chicago! The Colombian-American singer looked like a dream in an all-white outfit, and her voice was as smooth as honey. She sang hits like "Telepatía" and "Moonlight" while dancers moved around her in perfect sync. Some routines even had chairs and mirror tricks — it felt like a movie. Kali told us she changed her entrance from a swing to a carriage as a nod to Selena's famous 1995 concert, but she made it her own. The best surprise? She revealed she has a whole album done! "It's in Spanglish," she said, mixing English and Spanish. She also shared why she picked Mariah the Scientist to join the tour: "I love her songwriting. This tour is for the girls!" Kali wants everyone to leave feeling inspired and proud of who they are. She came from humble beginnings and hopes her story encourages kids to believe in themselves. The tour will hit New York, Atlanta, and Los Angeles. So if you get a chance to go, expect a magical show — and maybe a sneak peek of new music!
why_it_matters: Kali's journey from humble beginnings to a carriage-riding star proves that believing in yourself and working hard can turn the biggest dreams into reality.

background_read: Kali Uchis is a Grammy-winning Colombian-American singer who mixes soul, R&B, and Latin music into her own style.
Sueños is a yearly music festival in Chicago that celebrates Latin music and brings together top artists from many Spanish-speaking countries.
Selena Quintanilla was a famous Mexican-American singer in the 1990s who is still an icon today, especially known for her powerful voice and stage presence.
Article_Structure: WHO: Kali Uchis, a Colombian-American superstar singer.
WHAT: She began her For the Girls tour by riding a carriage onstage, performed her hit songs, and surprised fans by revealing she has a finished Spanglish album.
WHERE: At the Sueños music festival in Chicago, Illinois.
WHY: To create a magical start for her tour, honor Selena Quintanilla, and inspire fans with her new music.

perspectives.description: Concertgoers were thrilled by the dramatic entrance and the surprise album news, making the event unforgettable.
Some critics might say a carriage onstage is a flashy trick that could take attention away from the music itself.
The tour's focus on female artists and the mix of Spanish and English highlight how Latin music keeps breaking boundaries worldwide.
